## Reproduction

While comparing the complete JavaScript template snapshot (tree 7877a27980664bc6453e80262f8391d1c2562ab1) against link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer#92, the downstream CI exposed two shared gaps:

1. `npm audit --json` in the root, `examples/universal-app`, and `.github/actions/artifact-transport` reports GHSA-g3hv-75wg-m249 for minimatch 7–10. The desktop graph also reports GHSA-3g3m-2fjr-6pw4 for glob 9–14.0.1. The advisory propagation reports nine desktop packages even though there are only two underlying causes. The default high-only gate remains green but emits warnings; the scheduled moderate/fixable gate can fail. Upstream fixes exist: minimatch >=11.0.1 and glob >=14.0.2.
2. `pipx run zizmor==1.30.1 --config .github/zizmor.yml --min-confidence low --persona regular .` reports self-repository warnings for the artifact adapter references in links.yml, security.yml and workflows.yml. The existing compatibility ignore covers release.yml, example-app.yml and action.yml only. Satisfying these warnings with `$/...` makes actionlint 1.7.12 reject the new syntax; rhysd/actionlint#711 and rhysd/actionlint#732 already track that parser gap.

Downstream evidence: https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/actions/runs/42067846815 and https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/actions/runs/42067847790 . Complete logs and machine-readable audit output are preserved in the downstream PR's dev/log/issues/92/pulls/93 folder.

## Workarounds and code suggestions

- Resolve vulnerable transitive ranges with scoped overrides (`minimatch@>=7 <11` to ^11.0.4; `glob@>=9 <=14.0.1` to ^14.0.2), regenerate committed locks, and exercise archive extraction, actual Electron ASAR packaging and the live artifact roundtrip. Preserve unaffected older callable APIs used by legacy dependencies instead of globally forcing every historical minimatch/glob major.
- Until actionlint supports self-repository syntax, extend the existing narrowly documented self-repository compatibility rule to the three affected workflow files. Keep every other zizmor audit enabled. Add a policy check that catches new unlisted adapter users; remove this exception and adopt `$/` once both tools support it. Switching to a maintained parser with full support is another longer-term option.
- Dependency review's default scorecard threshold also emits twenty warnings for low aggregate repository-maintenance scores of SDK transitive packages, independently of known vulnerabilities. Keep scores displayed as informational context (`show-openssf-scorecard: true`, `warn-on-openssf-scorecard-level: 0`) while retaining strict vulnerability enforcement and full npm-audit reporting. This avoids treating a heuristic repository score as a package vulnerability verdict.

References: https://github.com/isaacs/minimatch/security/advisories/GHSA-g3hv-75wg-m249 , https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-3g3m-2fjr-6pw4 , https://docs.zizmor.sh/audits/#self-repository .
title: CI audit: transitive advisories and incomplete local-action compatibility policy

body:
Found at `0a3957d8195271829aa3cd5adce58a98fe73be2b`, `scripts/create-github-release.mjs:99-115`, while auditing https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-sovereign/pull/55. The section scanner treats Markdown headings inside fenced example code as real release boundaries, silently deleting the rest of the notes.

Minimal CHANGELOG.md:

````markdown
## 1.2.3

Example:

```md
## 9.9.9
```

Remaining details.

## 1.2.2
old
````

Expected: the 1.2.3 body contains the whole fenced example and `Remaining details.`. Actual: the body ends at `Example:` and the opening fence, leaving invalid Markdown and dropping real release information. A requested version that appears only inside a fenced example can also select example text as release notes.

Reproduce from the template root (no real publishing):

```sh
node --input-type=module <<'JS'
import { extractReleaseNotes } from './scripts/create-github-release.mjs';
console.log(extractReleaseNotes('## 1.2.3\n\nExample:\n\n```md\n## 9.9.9\n```\n\nRemaining details.\n\n## 1.2.2\nold', '1.2.3'));
JS
```

The JS and Python snapshot functions were executed offline and both returned the truncated body. The Rust source has the same boundary error in `next_section_re`, which matches `^## [` without fence state; the above CLI reproduction uses a local gh stub. No Rust template build was run on the constrained downstream machine.

Workaround: use indented example code or avoid version-shaped headings inside fenced changelog examples until the scanner is fixed. Do not silently delete the example or the later prose from the actual release.

Suggested fix: find exact release headings only outside Markdown code fences (both backticks and tildes, matching closing delimiter/length), or parse Markdown to an AST and slice by top-level heading offsets. Preserve body bytes/indentation, fail explicitly on missing required entries, and add tests for a fenced next-version heading, a target version only inside a fence, CRLF and multiple change subsections. The downstream PR adds these regressions in `js/tests/ci-github-release.test.js` and fixes its shared release-content helper; the Rust/Python publication programs are template-specific and are not vendored into the product.
title: Release changelog extraction treats version headings inside fenced examples as release boundaries

body:
Audit of immutable template revision 16225e7f26006333bdb107cddb6d5d3e54b93723 while investigating konard/medical-speech-to-text#5 found these shared defects:

1. `scripts/check-mjs-syntax.sh` checks only top-level `*.mjs` in three directories. Stage `src/index.js` containing `const broken = ;`, a nested `.cjs` adapter, or a nested test `.mjs`: the gate exits zero. An empty inventory also passes. Discover tracked `.js/.mjs/.cjs` recursively, reject empty evidence, and check each file. Historical investigation data can be explicitly excluded.
2. `.github/codeql/codeql-config.yml` excludes all examples, including the shipped web, Electron and mobile application. Remove the blanket exclusion. Strengthen the existing structural test to require inclusion.
3. npm's install-script policy reports unreviewed optional `node-pty@1.1.0`; existing example approvals are not version pinned. Record explicit decisions for every `hasInstallScript` entry across platform-specific locks. Deny optional PTY when ordinary command execution suffices and pin approvals for the binaries actually used. Deno does not read npm's policy: its own `deno.json` requires `"allowScripts": {"deny": ["npm:node-pty@1.1.0"]}`. A clean Deno install reproduces the ignored-build warning until this independent decision is recorded.
4. The artifact SDK 6.3.1 resolves deprecated glob 10.5.0 through archiver-utils and its unzip-stream reader calls deprecated `Buffer()`. A real ZIP roundtrip under `node --pending-deprecation --throw-deprecation` fails at `unzip-stream/lib/unzip-stream.js:47`. A scoped glob 13.0.6 override preserves the consumer's sync API. Retain the official SDK's raw-download transport/digest checks and use zip.js 2.24.0 for streamed ZIP64 extraction. It has no runtime dependencies. The initial unzipper alias passed archive tests but introduced four low Scorecard dependencies, so it is not the recommended solution. Preserve CRC, traversal, symlink, binary/empty/nested-file and cleanup assertions plus a real GitHub upload/download/Pages roundtrip.
5. Desktop packaging installs deprecated glob 7/inflight through ASAR 3.4.1 and rimraf 2 through temp 0.9.4. Blanket glob/rimraf major overrides break callback APIs. A tested alternative upgrades ASAR itself to 4.3.1 and supplies a narrow native fs.rm adapter only for temp's four literal-path cleanup calls. Test actual app-builder-lib packing/extraction, electron-winstaller loading, async/sync temp cleanup, symlinks, literal brackets and refusal of unsupported options on the three supported platforms. All four local lockfiles now reject deprecated dependencies rather than allowlisting them.
6. Pages suppresses DEP0040 from deploy-pages v5's bundled punycode import. This is already tracked in https://github.com/actions/deploy-pages/issues/413. A process-scoped Node 24 module hook can supply pinned userland punycode 2.3.1, remove the warning filter and keep runtime deprecations fatal. Test conversion/error behavior and the unmodified immutable upstream bundle without credentials; it must still refuse missing OIDC configuration. Keep deployment permissions and preconditions intact.

7. Native Node fixtures run in every runtime leg, but Node setup/root npm installation previously excluded Deno. Pin Node 24 and install each native fixture's owning npm lock in every leg. Prepare Deno's frozen graph before the timed suite (`deno test -A --parallel --no-run --frozen`); run every test afterward under the original deadline. Cold registry work was included only in Deno's deadline, and Windows reported 75–77/100 seconds. Preserve the 100-second limit and 70-second early warning. A clean-worktree reproduction retains the real missing-dependency failure and complete prepared Deno suite.

Reproducing tests, explicit native adapter inventories, dependency research and complete verification evidence are in https://github.com/konard/medical-speech-to-text/pull/6 and its `dev/log/issues/5/pulls/6` directory. No acceptance behavior is removed and no publication/deployment is performed. The npm identity/bootstrap failure in that repository remains a separate maintainer configuration blocker.
title: CI audit: syntax and CodeQL coverage gaps, install-script policy and artifact deprecations

body:
## Summary

`extractReleaseNotes()` builds the version-header regex without an **end anchor** after the version, so extracting notes for `1.2` can match the section that actually belongs to `1.2.3` (a prefix match).

## Location

`scripts/create-github-release.mjs:95-96`

```js
const versionHeaderRegex = new RegExp(
  `## ${escapeRegex(version)}[\\s\\S]*?(?=## \\d|$)`
);
```

The `escapeRegex()` call (added to neutralize the `.` wildcard) is correct, but `## 1\.2` still matches at the start of a `## 1.2.3` header because nothing requires the version token to end.

## Reproduction

CHANGELOG:

```md
## 1.2.3
- newer notes

## 1.2
- older notes
```

`extractReleaseNotes(changelog, '1.2')` returns the **1.2.3** notes (it matches starting at `## 1.2.3`), publishing the wrong section for the `1.2` release.

## Suggested fix

Anchor the end of the version token:

```js
const versionHeaderRegex = new RegExp(
  `## ${escapeRegex(version)}(?=\\s|$)[\\s\\S]*?(?=## \\d|$)`
);
```

(The Rust template's `create-github-release.rs` is immune — it uses `(?m)^## \[{escaped}\]`, bracket-delimited and line-anchored.)

## Notes

Found while auditing the downstream `link-assistant/web-search` release pipeline (issue #17). The same unanchored pattern exists there and is being fixed; the Python/C# templates that derive their changelog extraction from this script likely share it.
title: extractReleaseNotes regex lacks end-anchor: '1.2' matches the '1.2.3' section

body:
## Summary

The `preview-regen` job in `.github/workflows/example-app.yml` installs the
Playwright Chromium browser with no per-step timeout, no retry, and no browser
cache. The Playwright CDN (`cdn.playwright.dev`) can stall a download after the
bytes finish transferring, with **no internal timeout**, hanging the step until
the job-level `timeout-minutes` fires. This wastes a full runner-timeout window
(~20 min) on every transient stall and re-downloads the ~170 MiB browser on
every run.

## Where

`.github/workflows/example-app.yml`, job `preview-regen`:

```yaml
- name: Install browser automation dependencies
  env:
    PLAYWRIGHT_SKIP_BROWSER_DOWNLOAD: '1'   # good: postinstall download skipped
  run: npm install --no-save --package-lock=false --no-audit --no-fund browser-commander@0.8.1 playwright@1.59.1

- name: Install Chromium for preview rendering
  run: npx playwright install --with-deps chromium   # <-- no timeout, no retry, no cache
```

The `PLAYWRIGHT_SKIP_BROWSER_DOWNLOAD: '1'` guard on the npm install is correct,
but the subsequent explicit `npx playwright install` is unguarded.

## Impact observed downstream

We hit this exact stall in `link-assistant/hive-mind` (a near-identical
preview-regen + e2e Pages workflow modelled on this template): the Chromium
download reached 100% of 170.4 MiB, then the connection stalled on the next
asset with no timeout and the job hung for ~22 minutes before the runner
cancelled it.

## Suggested fix

Two complementary mitigations (both already validated downstream):

1. **Cache the browser** so most runs skip the download entirely:

```yaml
- name: Cache Playwright browsers
  uses: actions/cache@v4
  with:
    path: ~/.cache/ms-playwright
    key: playwright-1.59.1-${{ runner.os }}
```

2. **Wrap the install in a `timeout` + retry loop** so a transient stall
   self-heals instead of consuming the whole job window:

```yaml
- name: Install Chromium for preview rendering (retry on stalled download)
  run: |
    for attempt in 1 2 3; do
      if timeout 360 npx playwright install --with-deps chromium; then
        echo "Playwright Chromium installed on attempt $attempt"
        exit 0
      fi
      echo "::warning::Playwright install attempt $attempt failed or timed out; retrying in 10s"
      sleep 10
    done
    echo "::error::Playwright Chromium install failed after 3 attempts"
    exit 1
```

Pinning the cache key to the Playwright version (`playwright-1.59.1-...`) keeps
the cache correct across upgrades.

## Context

Reported while comparing CI/CD workflows in `link-assistant/hive-mind` against
this template (link-assistant/hive-mind#1838). Happy to open a PR with the fix
if useful.
title: preview-regen: guard Playwright Chromium install with timeout+retry and cache (CDN can stall with no internal timeout)
